metadata.scope: Whole backend repository: app/ (30.8k LOC, 339 HTTP endpoints across 29 routers), configuration, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, render.yaml, migrations (inventory only), scripts/ (import tooling), tests/.
metadata.exclusions: Frontends (Ignition-AdminFrontend, Ignition-StudentDashboard, Ignition-Landing), the landing site's /api/revalidate and /api/preview handlers, Cloudinary/Neon/Render account configuration, production runtime. No production or third-party system was contacted; all verification ran against the local ignition_test database inside a rolled-back transaction.

remediation.result: All 18 findings addressed; security suite 30/30, main suite 515 passed; pip-audit 0 known vulnerabilities (65 packages); bandit 0 high, 4 medium (xlsx import XML parsing, admin-only and disabled in production).

findings.title: Simulated portal checkout is enabled by default in production, so any student can unlock the paid portal without paying
findings.cwe: CWE-1188: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource (with CWE-840 Business Logic Errors)
findings.owasp_api: API6:2023 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows; API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration
findings.evidence: Settings.SIMULATED_PAYMENTS defaults to True (config.py:40). The production validator (_validate_secrets, config.py:141) checks the JWT secret and Cloudinary keys but never SIMULATED_PAYMENTS, and render.yaml does not set it, so a production deploy from the Blueprint runs with True. checkout_my_portal_access (student.py:2052) only refuses when the flag is False; otherwise it writes a COMPLETED PORTAL_ACCESS Payment (student.py:2072). PortalAccessService.has_access returns True for any COMPLETED PORTAL_ACCESS payment, which is exactly what _assert_entitled (document.py:99) checks before releasing offer and CAS letters.
findings.preconditions: Any self-registered student account (registration is public). Production deployed without SIMULATED_PAYMENTS=false in the environment.
findings.attack_scenario: A student registers, calls POST /student/me/access/checkout with {"payment_method":"esewa"}, receives has_access=true, and downloads their offer/CAS letters without paying the access fee.
findings.impact: Complete bypass of the portal access fee, which is the product's paywall, and loss of that revenue. The simulated payment rows are marked SIMULATED in reference and remarks, so finance can spot them afterwards, but access is already granted.
findings.reproduction: security-audit/tests/security/test_audit_findings.py::test_fapi_sec_001_production_refuses_simulated_payments and ::test_fapi_sec_001_checkout_unlocks_gated_documents_without_payment (both FAIL on the audited commit: production Settings boot with SIMULATED_PAYMENTS=True; checkout returns 200).
findings.root_cause: A demo-only switch fails open: its safe value has to be set explicitly, and nothing forces that in production.
findings.remediation: Make production refuse to boot while SIMULATED_PAYMENTS is true (or default it to False and enable it only in development/test), and set SIMULATED_PAYMENTS=false in render.yaml. Consider also refusing checkout when ENVIRONMENT=production regardless of the flag until a real gateway is integrated.
findings.patch:
--- a/app/core/config.py
+++ b/app/core/config.py
@@ def _validate_secrets(self) -> Settings:
         if self.ENVIRONMENT == "production":
+            if self.SIMULATED_PAYMENTS:
+                raise ValueError("SIMULATED_PAYMENTS must be false in production (no gateway is integrated).")
             if not self.JWT_SECRET_KEY:
--- a/render.yaml
+++ b/render.yaml
       - key: ENVIRONMENT
         value: production
+      - key: SIMULATED_PAYMENTS
+        value: "false"
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED 2026-09-26. SIMULATED_PAYMENTS defaults to False; production refuses to boot with it true; checkout also refuses whenever ENVIRONMENT=production; render.yaml sets it false. Tests: tests/test_security_audit_findings.py::test_fapi_sec_001_* PASS; tests/test_security_hardening.py::test_simulated_payments_are_off_by_default, ::test_production_refuses_to_boot_with_simulated_payments PASS. Live smoke: checkout -> 400.

findings.title: Checklist items accept any document_id: students can self-verify requirements and link other students' documents
findings.cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key; CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization
findings.owasp_api: API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization; API6:2023 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
findings.evidence: A student may PATCH document_id (_STUDENT_EDITABLE_CHECKLIST_FIELDS, workflow.py:485). ChecklistService.update_item loads the document by id (workflow_service.py:650) but checks neither its owner nor its type. If the document is already APPROVED, the item is set to VERIFIED (workflow_service.py:655), and link_to_application then files the document on the application (workflow_service.py:664). The student's application-documents list selects linked documents by application_id only (student.py:893), not by Document.student_id, so the linked foreign document's metadata is returned to the caller.
findings.preconditions: Authenticated student with an application that has a checklist item. Self-verification needs nothing more than any of their own APPROVED documents. Cross-student linking also needs another student's document UUID (random UUIDv4, so hard to obtain).
findings.attack_scenario: (a) A student whose 'photo' was approved links it to the 'passport' checklist item; the item is VERIFIED immediately and no reviewer ever sees a passport. (b) With a leaked document id, a student links another applicant's approved passport to their own application; it shows as verified evidence and its title, filename, remarks and status appear in the attacker's application view.
findings.impact: The document-review workflow can be bypassed: staff see VERIFIED requirements that were never reviewed for that purpose. It also allows cross-student linking and disclosure of another student's document metadata (the file bytes stay protected by the owner check on /documents/{id}/download).
findings.reproduction: test_fapi_sec_002_student_cannot_link_another_students_document (FAIL: status=200, item status=verified) and test_fapi_sec_002_approved_document_of_other_type_does_not_self_verify (FAIL: item VERIFIED).
findings.root_cause: The child resource (document) named in the request body is trusted without checking that it belongs to the same student as the parent application, and without checking that its type matches what the item requested.
findings.remediation: In update_application_checklist_item, resolve the document and require document.student_id == application.student_id (404 otherwise). Require document.document_type to match item.document_type when the item names one. Only auto-VERIFY when the approval came from staff for this same requirement; otherwise land SUBMITTED. Also restrict the student application-documents list to Document.student_id == application.student_id as defence in depth.
findings.patch:
--- a/app/routes/workflow.py
+++ b/app/routes/workflow.py
@@ async def update_application_checklist_item(
-    await _assert_application_access(application_id, user, application_service)
+    application = await _assert_application_access(application_id, user, application_service)
@@
     data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+    if data.get("document_id") is not None:
+        document = await DocumentService(application_service.session).get_document(data["document_id"])
+        if document is None or document.student_id != application.student_id:
+            raise NotFoundException("Document not found")
+        if item.document_type is not None and document.document_type is not item.document_type:
+            raise BadRequestException("That document is not the type this item asks for")
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Checklist PATCH requires document.student_id == application.student_id (404) and a matching document_type (400) for students AND staff; auto-VERIFY only when the approved document's type matches the item (custom items: staff only). Student application-documents list filtered on Document.student_id. Tests: test_fapi_sec_002_* PASS; hardening tests for the staff path and the legitimate verify path PASS.

findings.title: Workflow step ids are not tied to the application in the URL (cross-application read and write)
findings.cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
findings.evidence: Each handler authorises the caller against application_id (_assert_application_access) and then acts on step_id with get_step(step_id)/list_activities(step_id), which filter on the step id only. Nothing checks that the step's ApplicationWorkflow.application_id equals the application_id in the path.
findings.preconditions: Student: owns any application and knows another application's step UUID. Staff (admin/counsellor): can already reach any application through these routes (see FAPI-SEC-005), so the extra exposure is mostly for students.
findings.attack_scenario: A student calls GET /applications/{own_app}/workflow/steps/{victim_step}/activities and reads staff comments and status history on another student's workflow.
findings.impact: Cross-student disclosure of workflow activity (staff comments). Counsellors can also change steps of applications outside their own-work scope. Likelihood is limited because step ids are random UUIDs that are only shown to people who can already see that workflow.
findings.root_cause: The parent/child relationship is checked for the parent only; the child lookup is not scoped to the parent.
findings.remediation: Add ApplicationWorkflowService.get_step_for_application(step_id, application_id), which joins ApplicationWorkflow and filters on application_id, and use it in all three step routes. Return 404 on mismatch.
findings.patch:
+    async def get_step_for_application(self, step_id: UUID, application_id: UUID) -> ApplicationWorkflowStep | None:
+        return await self.session.scalar(
+            select(ApplicationWorkflowStep)
+            .join(ApplicationWorkflow, ApplicationWorkflow.id == ApplicationWorkflowStep.application_workflow_id)
+            .where(ApplicationWorkflowStep.id == step_id, ApplicationWorkflow.application_id == application_id)
+        )
# routes/workflow.py: replace get_step(step_id) with get_step_for_application(step_id, application_id) and 404 on None,
# including before list_activities(step_id).
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. ApplicationWorkflowService.get_step_for_application joins ApplicationWorkflow on application_id; used by PATCH step, GET activities and POST comment (404 on mismatch). Tests: test_fapi_sec_003_* and test_a_step_cannot_be_updated_through_another_application PASS.

findings.title: Client-supplied application_id and intake_id are not ownership-checked when documents, threads and applications are created
findings.cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
findings.evidence: upload_document forces student_id to the caller for students but passes the form's application_id straight to DocumentService.create_document, which inserts an ApplicationDocument link (document_service.py:70) with no ownership check. create_my_thread passes payload.application_id into create_thread unchecked. create_my_application stores payload.intake_id without checking that it belongs to payload.program_id. A nonexistent id raises an IntegrityError, which returns 500.
findings.preconditions: Authenticated student who knows another student's application UUID.
findings.attack_scenario: A student uploads a file with application_id set to a victim's application. The file then appears in the victim's 'documents filed against this application' view and on the staff side of that application. A thread can be filed against the victim's application in the same way.
findings.impact: Integrity: unsolicited content (possibly malicious files) planted on another applicant's file, where staff and the victim will open it. There is no read access to the victim's data. Likelihood is low because application ids are random UUIDs.
findings.root_cause: Body/form foreign keys to parent resources are trusted; only the path parameters go through ownership checks.
findings.remediation: When application_id is supplied, load the application and require application.student_id == student_id (for staff uploads too), returning 404 otherwise. For student threads use repo.get_or_404(Application, payload.application_id). Validate that intake_id belongs to program_id.
findings.patch:
--- a/app/routes/document.py
+++ b/app/routes/document.py
@@ async def upload_document(
     if user.role is UserRole.STUDENT:
         student_id = user.id
+    if application_id is not None:
+        application = await ApplicationService(service.session).get_application(application_id)
+        if application is None or application.student_id != student_id:
+            raise NotFoundException("Application not found")
--- a/app/routes/student.py (create_my_thread)
+    if payload.application_id is not None:
+        await StudentScopedRepository(service.session, student).get_or_404(Application, payload.application_id)
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Upload: application must belong to student_id (staff too), staff target must be a student (or self); student thread: application via StudentScopedRepository; student create: intake must belong to program; staff application create/update validate student/counsellor/program/intake; staff thread create validates ids agree; POST /documents refuses a stored file owned by another student; global IntegrityError -> 409. Tests: test_fapi_sec_004_* and 6 hardening tests PASS.

findings.title: Counsellor own-work scoping is not enforced on the /communication router or the application workflow/checklist routes
findings.evidence: The codebase defines a privacy rule: a counsellor sees their own records plus unclaimed ones (api/scoping.py:45, services/message_scope.py:41). It is enforced on /applications/{id} (application.py:53), /leads and the legacy /messages router. The /communication router, which replaces /messages, never applies it: staff_inbox takes no user and returns every thread, list_student_threads defaults include_internal=True, and get_thread only checks the role (communication.py:247). _assert_application_access returns any application for any APPLICATION_STAFF_ROLES member (workflow.py:79) without may_see_record, although GET /applications/{id} returns 404 for the same caller.
findings.attack_scenario: Counsellor A opens /communication/threads or /communication/students/{id}/threads for a student counselled by counsellor B and reads the whole correspondence, including INTERNAL staff notes. The same counsellor reads and edits the workflow and checklist of B's applications, even though /applications/{id} hides them.
findings.impact: Confidentiality breach of student correspondence, which the code itself calls 'the clearest privacy failure in the console'. Internal notes are exposed across the counsellor team, and the scoping on /applications is undone by the sub-resources.
findings.reproduction: test_fapi_sec_005_other_counsellors_student_correspondence (FAIL: 2 threads incl. internal; inbox shows 2), test_fapi_sec_005_checklist_of_other_counsellors_application (FAIL: 200), and positive control test_fapi_sec_005_control_application_is_hidden_from_other_counsellor (PASS: 404).
findings.root_cause: Scoping is applied per router rather than centrally, and the new router and the sub-resource helper were written without it.
findings.remediation: Add a thread-level visibility condition (own student, own lead, own application, already replied, or unclaimed) to staff_inbox, threads_for_student/lead/application and the by-id thread and attachment checks for non-admin roles. Return 404 when it fails. In _assert_application_access, call may_see_record(user, application.counsellor_id) for staff and return 404 when it fails. Add scoping tests mirroring tests/test_scoping.py for these routes.
findings.patch:
--- a/app/routes/workflow.py
+++ b/app/routes/workflow.py
@@ async def _assert_application_access(
-    if user.role in APPLICATION_STAFF_ROLES:
-        return application
+    if user.role in APPLICATION_STAFF_ROLES:
+        if not may_see_record(user, application.counsellor_id):
+            raise NotFoundException("Application not found")
+        return application
# communication: pass `user` into staff_inbox/threads_for_* and AND a visibility clause
# derived from message_scope.visible_students_condition (keyed on MessageThread.student_id / lead.assigned_to).
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. _assert_application_access applies may_see_record (404) for staff; /communication applies message_scope.visible_threads_condition to inbox, student/lead/application lists, by-id thread, reply and attachments; thread creation limited to own/unclaimed targets; /workflow-steps scoped. Tests: test_fapi_sec_005_* PASS (control still PASS) plus 5 hardening tests.

findings.title: Leave-request attachments (e.g. medical notes) are uploaded as public Cloudinary assets
findings.cwe: CWE-552: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
findings.owasp_api: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (data exposure); API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration
findings.evidence: store_upload defaults to private=False, which uploads as type='upload' (public, CDN-served, no signature). create_leave_request calls it without private=True (leave.py:132) and stores the returned public secure_url. The uploads module states that CONTENT_FOLDER is 'the one folder uploaded with private=False'; leave attachments contradict that design.
findings.preconditions: Anyone who obtains the URL: browser history, logs, referrers, a forwarded link, or any manager/admin viewing the request.
findings.attack_scenario: A leave request's attachment URL is copied into a chat or ticket. Anyone holding it can fetch the employee's medical certificate indefinitely, with no authentication and no expiry.
findings.impact: Exposure of employee health data. Likelihood is low because the object name is a random UUID, but there is no access control at all once the URL is known.
findings.reproduction: test_fapi_sec_006_leave_attachment_is_private (FAIL: attachment_url returned, which store_upload only does for public uploads).
findings.root_cause: A default-public storage helper was used for a sensitive document class.
findings.remediation: Upload leave attachments with private=True into LEAVE_ATTACHMENT_FOLDER, store stored_file_name instead of a URL, and serve them through an authenticated route that checks self-or-MANAGE_ROLES before minting a signed URL. Migrate existing assets to the authenticated delivery type. Consider making store_upload's private parameter keyword-required with no default.
findings.patch:
--- a/app/routes/leave.py
+++ b/app/routes/leave.py
-        stored = await store_upload(file, DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS, folder=LEAVE_ATTACHMENT_FOLDER)
-        attachment_url = stored.url
+        stored = await store_upload(file, DOCUMENT_EXTENSIONS, folder=LEAVE_ATTACHMENT_FOLDER, private=True)
+        attachment_url = f"/api/v1/leave-requests/{{id}}/attachment"  # authenticated, owner-or-manager
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Leave attachments uploaded private=True into attachment_stored_file_name (migration b4e1d9c2a7f3); attachment_url is never returned; owner-or-manager routes GET /leave-requests/{id}/attachment[/link]; store_upload's private flag is now keyword-required with no default. Legacy assets: run scripts/migrate_leave_attachments_private.py --apply. Tests: test_fapi_sec_006_* and test_leave_attachment_is_owner_or_manager_only PASS.

findings.title: Pagination parameters are unbounded and unvalidated on about 45 list endpoints
findings.cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling; CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
affected_endpoints: Every authenticated list route declaring `page: int = 1, limit: int = N` without Query(ge/le): users, documents, documents/folders, applications, leads, appointments, payments, tasks, notifications, content-*, catalogue, academic, attendance, leave, payroll, activity-logs, workflow, student/me/* lists (see endpoint-security-matrix.csv)
affected_code: app/routes/public.py:88 (the correct pattern, used only on /public)
findings.evidence: Only /public/* and /communication/threads constrain limit with Query(ge=1, le=100). Everywhere else limit and page are plain ints passed straight into .limit()/.offset((page-1)*limit). page=0 produces a negative OFFSET: asyncpg raises InvalidRowCountInResultOffsetClauseError, which becomes a 500. limit=1000000 is accepted.
findings.preconditions: Any authenticated user (students included for the /student/me/* and shared lists).
findings.attack_scenario: A script repeatedly calls list endpoints with limit=1000000 (for example /documents/folders, /content-pages or the /student/me/* lists), forcing large serialisations and database scans; page=0 or negative limits generate 500s and error-log noise.
findings.impact: Availability and cost: memory and CPU spikes on a small Render instance, plus log flooding.
findings.root_cause: The clamping convention was applied to the public router only, not project-wide.
findings.remediation: Move PageParam/LimitParam (ge=1, le=100) from routes/public.py into a shared module and use them on every list route. Also clamp inside StudentScopedRepository.list and the services as defence in depth.
findings.patch:
# app/api/pagination.py
+PageParam = Annotated[int, Query(ge=1)]
+LimitParam = Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=100)]
# every list route:
-    page: int = 1,
-    limit: int = 20,
+    page: PageParam = 1,
+    limit: LimitParam = 20,
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Shared app/api/pagination.py (page 1..10000, limit 1..200 — 200 because the consoles request it); applied to every list route incl. /public page and /communication; clamp in StudentScopedRepository; year/month bounded. Build-time guard test_every_paginated_route_bounds_page_and_limit. Tests: test_fapi_sec_007_* PASS. Live: limit=1000000 and page=0 -> 422.

findings.title: Unpublished CMS and catalogue drafts are readable by any authenticated account, including self-registered students
findings.evidence: The staff CMS and catalogue read routes depend only on get_current_user and accept is_published=None/False. Because /auth/register is public, 'authenticated' effectively means 'anyone'. Writes are correctly limited to admin/marketing.
findings.attack_scenario: A competitor registers a student account and lists /content-pages?is_published=false and /scholarships to read embargoed pages, draft pricing and unpublished scholarships before launch.
findings.impact: Early disclosure of unpublished marketing and catalogue content. No personal data is involved.
findings.root_cause: The staff console's read routes use the weakest authentication dependency.
findings.remediation: Guard these reads with require_staff (or the same admin/marketing role set as the writes). Students already have published-only equivalents under /public and /student/catalog.
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. CMS and catalogue read routes require_staff; workflow-template reads require_staff; academic /universities /programs /intakes return published-only rows to students. Tests: test_fapi_sec_008_* and 2 hardening tests PASS. Live: student GET /content-pages -> 403.

findings.title: Account e-mail handling: case-sensitive uniqueness, unverified self-service e-mail change, duplicate address returns 500
findings.cwe: CWE-178: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity; CWE-620: Unverified Password Change (analogous, e-mail); CWE-755
findings.evidence: users.email is a case-sensitive UNIQUE column and lookups compare it exactly. Pydantic EmailStr only lowercases the domain, so 'Sec.Case@x' and 'sec.case@x' become two accounts. PATCH /users/me accepts a new email with no current-password confirmation and no verification (email_verified_at is never written), and a taken address hits the DB constraint, giving an unhandled IntegrityError and a 500.
findings.preconditions: Any account. The takeover-persistence variant needs a stolen access token.
findings.attack_scenario: Someone with a briefly hijacked access token changes the account's e-mail, which becomes a permanent pivot once a reset/recovery flow is added. Separately, a person registers the case-variant of a known applicant's address so staff see two 'same' people; squatting on addresses is possible because registration never verifies them.
findings.impact: Identity confusion and duplicate accounts. It weakens future account-recovery flows, and the 500s disclose the existence of addresses.
findings.root_cause: E-mail is treated as an opaque string, and identity changes are not treated as security-sensitive.
findings.remediation: Normalise e-mail to lower-case at every entry point and add a unique index on lower(email) via migration. Require current_password (and ideally re-verification) to change e-mail. Catch IntegrityError and return 409. Add e-mail verification at registration before the account can hold applications.
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. All inbound e-mails trimmed+lower-cased (schemas/email.py); lookups compare lower(email); unique index uq_users_email_lower (model + migration with dedupe guard, verified on Postgres 16); self e-mail change needs current_password (per-account throttled); duplicates -> 409. E-mail verification remains a product backlog item (no mail infrastructure). Tests: test_fapi_sec_009_* and 3 hardening tests PASS.

findings.title: Rate limits and audit IPs are keyed on the reverse proxy's address, not the client's
findings.cwe: CWE-348: Use of Less Trusted Source; CWE-770
findings.owasp_api: API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption; API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration
findings.evidence: slowapi uses get_remote_address, i.e. request.client.host. The container starts `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` with no --forwarded-allow-ips, and uvicorn 0.52 trusts X-Forwarded-For only from FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (default 127.0.0.1, uvicorn/config.py:357), which render.yaml does not set. Behind Render's proxy, request.client.host is therefore the proxy's address for every client.
findings.preconditions: Deployment behind Render's (or any) reverse proxy whose address is not 127.0.0.1. Must be confirmed by logging request.client.host in production.
findings.attack_scenario: An anonymous caller sends 10 login attempts a minute and exhausts the shared bucket, so every legitimate user gets 429 at login. Six eligibility submissions a minute shut down the public lead funnel in the same way. Activity logs record the proxy IP for every login, which defeats forensics.
findings.impact: A cheap denial of service against authentication and lead capture, and loss of source-IP attribution in the security audit trail. Per-attacker throttling also becomes meaningless: the limits only work globally.
findings.reproduction: Environment-dependent. Verification: in production, log request.client.host and X-Forwarded-For for a request and confirm they differ; or send 11 logins from one IP and confirm a second IP is also rate-limited.
findings.root_cause: Proxy-aware client IP resolution is not configured.
findings.remediation: Run uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=<Render's proxy CIDR> (or '*' only if the container is unreachable except through the proxy), and keep get_remote_address. Add per-account limits on login in addition to per-IP limits.
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED IN CODE, CONFIRM AFTER DEPLOY. core/client_ip.py resolves the client from X-Forwarded-For counted from the right (TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS, render.yaml=1; uvicorn '*' deliberately not used because it trusts the spoofable leftmost entry); used by slowapi and all audit IPs; invalid values fall back to the peer. Verify with GET /api/v1/health/client-ip as super_admin. Unit tests for spoofing/garbage PASS.

findings.title: Account lockout enables targeted lockout of any account and confirms which e-mails are registered
findings.cwe: CWE-645: Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism; CWE-204: Observable Response Discrepancy
findings.evidence: Five wrong passwords lock any account for 15 minutes, keyed on the account alone. A locked account answers 403 'Account temporarily locked', while an unknown address always answers 400 'Invalid email or password', so the lock message confirms that the address exists. The code equalises bcrypt timing for this purpose, but the lock message undoes it. Registration also returns 409 for existing addresses.
findings.preconditions: Knowledge of a target e-mail (for example staff addresses on the website).
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker sends 5 bad passwords for every counsellor's address every 15 minutes, keeping the whole console locked out. The 403-vs-400 difference enumerates staff accounts.
findings.impact: Denial of service against specific users and e-mail enumeration.
findings.reproduction: test_fapi_sec_011_locked_account_is_indistinguishable_from_unknown (FAIL: locked=403 'Account temporarily locked...' vs unknown=400 'Invalid email or password').
findings.root_cause: Lockout keyed on the account alone, with a distinguishable response.
findings.remediation: Return the same status and message for locked, wrong-password and unknown-account cases; notify the account owner out of band. Prefer progressive delays or a CAPTCHA keyed on account plus IP over a hard lock. Accept 409 on register as a product trade-off or move to verify-by-email signup.
findings.patch:
-            raise ForbiddenException("Account temporarily locked due to failed login attempts")
+            verify_password(password, _dummy_hash())
+            return None  # indistinguishable from a bad password; alert the owner out of band
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Locked, throttled, wrong-password and unknown accounts all return 400 'Invalid email or password' with a bcrypt round; tier 1 throttle per (account, IP) in Redis (5/15 min); tier 2 account-wide lock at 20 failures with an in-app notification to the owner. Tests: test_fapi_sec_011_* and 3 lockout tests PASS. Live: Redis keys hashed, TTL 900s.

findings.title: Uploads are read fully into memory before the size check, with no request-body cap
findings.evidence: store_upload does `content = await file.read()` and only then compares len(content) with MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB (25). No middleware or server limit caps the request body, and a single message may carry 10 attachments plus a voice note, all held in memory at once.
findings.attack_scenario: A few concurrent multipart requests carrying 10 x 200 MB parts each push the 'starter' Render instance into memory exhaustion before any size check runs.
findings.impact: Availability. The actual ceiling depends on Render's proxy body limit, which was not verified.
findings.reproduction: Not executed (would be a DoS test). Code-level evidence only; verify Render's max request size.
findings.root_cause: Size is validated after buffering rather than while streaming.
findings.remediation: Reject on Content-Length over the limit early (middleware); read UploadFile in chunks and abort once the limit is exceeded; set a proxy or server body cap; lower MAX_ATTACHMENTS or cap the total size per message.
findings.patch:
+    chunks, total = [], 0
+    while chunk := await file.read(1024 * 1024):
+        total += len(chunk)
+        if total > limit:
+            raise BadRequestException(...)
+        chunks.append(chunk)
+    content = b"".join(chunks)
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. BodySizeLimitMiddleware rejects Content-Length > MAX_REQUEST_BODY_MB (60) and cuts off streamed bodies at the limit (413); store_upload reads in 1 MB chunks and aborts at MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB. Tests: 3 hardening tests PASS. Live: 999999999-byte Content-Length -> 413 with CORS headers.

findings.title: Signed Cloudinary delivery URLs for private documents never expire
findings.evidence: The code documents this itself: cloudinary_url ignores expires_at for the authenticated delivery type without token auth, so a minted URL is a permanent bearer credential.
findings.preconditions: A signed URL leaks (history, logs, referrer, forwarding).
findings.attack_scenario: A passport scan's signed URL pasted into a support ticket stays valid forever.
findings.impact: Long-lived access to private documents after a URL leaks.
findings.root_cause: Cloudinary token-based authentication is not enabled.
findings.remediation: Enable Cloudinary token-based auth (auth_token with a short duration) for the authenticated type, or proxy file bytes through the API with Cache-Control: private, no-store.
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED (opt-in). CLOUDINARY_AUTH_TOKEN_KEY enables expiring __cld_token__ URLs (verified the SDK needs sign_url=True with auth_token); redirects and all API responses default to Cache-Control no-store. Requires enabling token auth on the Cloudinary account. Test test_private_links_carry_an_expiring_token_when_configured PASS.

findings.title: Counsellors can read and edit any student's profile and documents regardless of assignment
findings.evidence: The documented own-work rule (api/scoping.py) covers leads, applications and threads only. Profiles (passport and citizenship numbers, family and addresses) and documents are open to every counsellor.
findings.attack_scenario: A counsellor browses passport numbers of students assigned to colleagues.
findings.impact: Over-broad internal access to PII. This is a policy decision, not a code defect, but it is inconsistent with FAPI-SEC-005's rule.
findings.root_cause: Scoping policy is defined per surface.
findings.remediation: Decide the policy explicitly; if own-work applies to people, apply may_see_record-style checks (student's assigned counsellor) in student_profile and document staff branches.
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED (policy applied). api/scoping.student_visibility_condition / may_see_student (own or unclaimed, counsellor only) applied to /users/{id}/student-profile|education|experience|research|shortlist, /documents (list, folders, by-id, upload, create) and /users list/get/patch/avatar/enable-portal. Tests: 2 hardening tests PASS.

findings.title: Managers and admins can approve their own leave requests
findings.cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
findings.owasp_api: API6:2023 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
findings.evidence: approve_leave_request checks role and PENDING status but not request.user_id != user.id. The status check is not atomic, so there is also a double-approval race.
findings.attack_scenario: A manager submits and approves their own paid leave; attendance is marked as leave.
findings.impact: Segregation-of-duties gap in HR and payroll.
findings.remediation: Refuse approval or rejection when request.user_id == user.id (unless super_admin); use UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' to make the transition atomic.
findings.patch:
+    if request.user_id == user.id and user.role is not UserRole.SUPER_ADMIN:
+        raise ForbiddenException("You cannot review your own leave request")
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Review of one's own leave refused (403) except super_admin; approve/reject/cancel are single conditional UPDATEs (409 when the request already moved). Tests: 2 hardening tests PASS.

findings.title: Access tokens survive logout and password change; refresh rotation is not atomic
findings.cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration; CWE-367: TOCTOU
findings.evidence: Access JWTs carry no session id and are valid for 15 minutes after the sessions are revoked. refresh_tokens selects the session row without FOR UPDATE and then revokes it, so two concurrent refreshes with the same token can both succeed.
findings.preconditions: A stolen access token (15-minute window), or a racing refresh.
findings.attack_scenario: After the victim changes their password, an attacker's stolen access token keeps working for up to 15 minutes.
findings.impact: Short residual access; refresh-replay detection is weakened.
findings.root_cause: Stateless access tokens, and non-atomic rotation.
findings.remediation: Accept the 15-minute window or add a session id (sid) claim checked against user_sessions. Rotate with UPDATE ... WHERE revoked_at IS NULL RETURNING (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), and treat reuse of a revoked token as compromise (revoke the whole family).
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Access tokens carry sid; get_current_user requires a live user_sessions row (logout/password change/reset take effect immediately); refresh rotation is UPDATE..WHERE revoked_at IS NULL RETURNING; reuse outside a 10 s grace window revokes all sessions; logout by refresh token scoped to the caller; exp/sub required. Tests: 6 hardening tests PASS.

findings.title: The developer .env holds hosted Neon database and Cloudinary credentials under ENVIRONMENT=development
affected_code: .env (untracked; confirmed ignored by .gitignore:2 and .dockerignore:3; not present in git history)
findings.evidence: .env sets DATABASE_URL to a Neon host (*.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech/neondb) plus CLOUDINARY_* secrets, with ENVIRONMENT=development. Values were not printed. If this is the production database, a local run exposes production data through a development-mode server (/docs enabled, permissive LAN CORS regex, per-process JWT secret).
findings.preconditions: Developer machine compromise, or running dev tooling against production data.
findings.attack_scenario: A local `uvicorn --reload` bound to a LAN interface serves production data to any device on the network whose origin matches the dev CORS regex.
findings.impact: Production data exposure through development configuration.
findings.root_cause: The same hosted database and media account appear to serve development and production.
findings.remediation: Confirm whether this is the production database. Use a separate Neon branch or project and a separate Cloudinary environment for development; rotate the credentials if they are production ones.
findings.verification_after_fix: MITIGATED; OWNER ACTION REQUIRED. Settings repr now hides every credential (the old repr printed DATABASE_URL with password in tracebacks); startup warns when development points at a non-local database. Confirm whether the Neon DB in .env is production and, if so, create a dev branch and rotate the Neon password and Cloudinary keys.

findings.title: Anonymous eligibility submissions attach to existing leads matched by e-mail or phone
findings.cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow
findings.owasp_api: API6:2023 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
findings.evidence: submit() resolves an existing lead by e-mail or phone and attaches the new assessment to it (and fills lead.email when empty). The caller is anonymous and supplies both fields.
findings.preconditions: Knowledge of a lead's e-mail or phone.
findings.attack_scenario: Someone submits fabricated answers under a real prospect's phone number; the counsellor sees them on that person's lead. A phone of lead A combined with the e-mail of lead B can hit the unique e-mail index and return 500.
findings.impact: CRM data integrity. No data is disclosed (the response is deliberately narrow).
findings.root_cause: The identity of an anonymous submitter is inferred from self-asserted contact details.
findings.remediation: Always create a new assessment linked as 'unverified submission', and let staff merge it; or require e-mail confirmation before attaching to an existing lead.
findings.verification_after_fix: FIXED. Anonymous submissions matched to an existing lead no longer modify the lead and are logged as '(unverified)' on its timeline; lead conversion refuses staff accounts. Tests: 2 hardening tests PASS.
